---
title: "About"
---

I'm Emma Branch, an epidemiologist and data analyst, and a PhD candidate at the University of British Columbia. I mostly work in R, SAS, and SQL, and use Quarto, Shiny, and leaflet when the results need to be readable by actual humans.

I'm new to fisheries science. The quickest way I know to learn a field is to get my hands on its data, so I built this to get to grips with the basics (stock assessment, reference points, and DFO's Precautionary Approach). It also let me apply the habits I've picked up in health research: a tidy database with a data dictionary, rule-based checks, parameterised reports, and being upfront about what the data can't tell you.

This is an exploratory personal project. It isn't an official assessment, it doesn't reproduce any seafood recommendation program's methods, and it makes no recommendations. Any mistakes are mine, and corrections are very welcome through the GitHub repository.

## Code and data

All the code is on [GitHub](https://github.com/emmabranch/bc-fish-stock-status), and the processed data can be downloaded from the [Methods and data](methods.qmd#downloads) page.

## Other projects

- [BC Salmon Explorer](https://emmabranch.shinyapps.io/bc-salmon-explorer): an R Shiny app for exploring decades of BC salmon spawner counts.
- [BC lightstation sea temperatures](https://emmabranch.github.io/bc-lightstation-qc/): quality control and documentation of CIOOS lightstation data, including the 2014 to 2016 marine heatwave.
